  org_requires_sso boolean;
  has_sso boolean;

  end if;

  -- But RLS functions don't have direct access to the 'target row' easily without arguments.
  -- Alternative: Use a function that takes the org_id.

$$ language plpgsql security definer;

-- Helper function to check if a specific org requires SSO and if the current session has it
create or replace function public.is_org_sso_required(org_id bigint)
returns boolean as $$
declare
  requires_sso boolean;
  has_sso boolean;
begin
  -- Get org setting
  select into requires_sso require_sso from public.orgs where id = org_id;
  
  -- Default false if org not found
  if requires_sso is null then return true; end if;
  
  -- Check JWT amr claim for 'sso/saml'
  -- This is tricky in pure SQL without JSONB manipulation of the JWT payload which is not exposed directly.
  -- Supabase RLS allows checking JWT claims using the ->> operator on auth.jwt() in the policy itself.
  -- We don't need a function for the amr check, we can do it in the policy WHERE clause.
  return false; -- Org requires SSO, but we will verify in policy
end;
$$ language plpgsql security definer;

-- Enable RLS on all tables
alter table public.orgs enable row level security;
alter table public.org_members enable row level security;
alter table public.org_documents enable row level security;

-- Policy R5: Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything
create policy "Anonymous users cannot view or modify anything" on public.orgs for all using ( false );
create policy "Anonymous users cannot view or modify anything" on public.org_members for all using ( false );
create policy "Anonymous users cannot view or modify anything" on public.org_documents for all using ( false );

-- Policy R6: Service role has full access
create policy "Service role has full access" on public.orgs for all using ( auth.jwt() is not null and auth.role() = 'service_role' );
create policy "Service role has full access" on public.org_members for all using ( auth.jwt() is not null and auth.role() = 'service_role' );
create policy "Service role has full access" on public.org_documents for all using ( auth.jwt() is not null and auth.role() = 'service_role' );
